[D7:4] Deborah: Wow, cool that yoga has been helping you out! Do they also do yoga with you? Does your partner do yoga with you?
[D7:5] Jolene: He started joining me sometimes, which is nice for bonding and relaxing. It's brought us closer. This is just our random photo.
[D7:5] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a man and a woman holding hands with rings on them
[D7:6] Deborah: Aw, that's wonderful! How long have you been married?
[D7:7] Jolene: We're not married yet but we've been together for three years. We're taking it slow and loving the ride. This ring on his hand is just a decoration, not a wedding ring.
[D7:8] Deborah: Sounds nice, Jolene. Enjoying the journey is the main thing. So, how did you two meet?
[D7:9] Jolene: We actually met in an engineering class in college and quickly became friends. It eventually blossomed into something more and it's been great!
[D7:9] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a book and a calculator on a table
[D7:10] Deborah: Wow, your relationship started from a strong friendship. Do you still enjoy working on engineering projects together?
[D7:11] Jolene: Yep, teaming up for these projects feels great! We get each other's struggles and both love it.
[D7:11] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a group of men standing in front of a building
[D7:12] Deborah: Have yoga or meditation helped with any stress?
[D7:13] Jolene: Whenever I'm overwhelmed, I just take a break and do some breathing or meditate. It really helps me feel calmer and clearer, so I'm able to handle challenges more easily.
[D7:14] Deborah: It's been great to see your progress since we last chatted - keep it up!
[D7:15] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! Your support really means a lot. I'm gonna keep pushing forward and continue taking time for myself.

Session date: 7:03 pm on 1 February, 2023
[D3:4] Deborah: That's awesome, Jolene! You're enjoying the process. It must be really satisfying to see it come together. Keep up the good work! Oh, by the way, I met my new neighbor Anna yesterday!
[D3:4] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a yellow sign with a picture of a family

[D3:6] Deborah: It happened at yoga in the park.
[D3:7] Jolene: Wow, that's awesome! It's great connecting with people who have similar interests. Did you two talk about it?
[D3:8] Deborah: Yeah, we talked about how it has improved our lives and the sense of community it gives.
[D3:9] Jolene: Sounds great!
[D3:9] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a purse with a plant on a table
[D3:10] Deborah: Have you ever thought about resuming yoga?

Session date: 9:48 am on 4 February, 2023
[D4:1] Jolene: Hey Deborah! Good to hear from you. How've you been? I've been on an emotional rollercoaster lately, but I'm coping.
[D4:2] Deborah: Hey Jolene! Good to hear from you. All good here - how about you? Anything new happening lately?
[D4:3] Jolene: I had a major milestone last week and it went really well - I'm so relieved and proud. It was a huge accomplishment for me as an engineer.
[D4:4] Deborah: That's awesome. You must have worked really hard for that. I'm so proud of you. Care to share more about it?
[D4:5] Jolene: Thanks so much! I had to plan and research a lot to design and build a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need. It was tough, but I loved the experience.
[D4:6] Deborah: Your engineering skills really made a difference for people in a rural area. That's amazing! How did it feel when you saw it working?
[D4:7] Jolene: It was such a surreal moment. Seeing it working and providing clean water to the community was incredibly satisfying. It reminded me of how engineering can make a difference in people's lives. It made me feel like I had a purpose and had done something good.
[D4:8] Deborah: So, what are your career aspirations now?
[D4:9] Jolene:  I want to keep working in engineering and continue to make a positive impact on communities in need by creating sustainable solutions. My goal is to contribute towards making the world a better place with my work.
[D4:10] Deborah:  I'm sure great things will keep coming your way. Keep up the good work and follow your passions!
[D4:11] Jolene: Your support means a lot. I'm determined to keep going and make a difference. Your encouragement really motivates me to pursue my passions.
[D4:12] Deborah: When things get tough, just take a deep breath and remember why you're doing this. This is where I spend a lot of my time, teaching yoga. It's a great way to find balance and reconnect with ourselves. I bonded with Anna during yesterday's l yoga class.
[D4:12] Image caption (automatic): a photo of two women in a dance studio doing a dance pose
[D4:13] Jolene: Wow, that's awesome! What new poses did you try?
[D4:14] Deborah: We were trying out different dance poses, like Warrior II, which builds strength and boosts focus.
[D4:14] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman doing a yoga pose on a chair
[D4:15] Jolene: Is it difficult to do?
[D4:16] Deborah: Yes, but this brought us closer to Anna! We supported each other, that means a lot.
[D4:17] Jolene: Can you explain how to do it?
[D4:18] Deborah: Sure! To do this modified pose, sit on the edge of a chair with your feet planted. Twist your torso to one side and use your hand on your knee for support. You'll feel a stretch in your back and shoulders as you hold it for a few breaths, then switch sides. It's great for relaxing tense muscles.
[D4:19] Jolene: Sounds really hard! Here's my bookshelf!
[D4:19] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a book shelf with a lot of books on it
[D4:20] Deborah: That's quite a collection! Have you had a favorite book lately? I'd love to hear your thoughts.
[D4:21] Jolene: Thanks Deborah! I'm really into this book called "Sapiens" - it's a fascinating look at human history and how technology has affected us. It's giving me a lot to think about!
[D4:22] Deborah: Great, this is interesting! Have you come across any recent ones that really struck you?
[D4:23] Jolene: Two weeks ago I read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting! 
[D4:24] Deborah: That sounds cool, Jolene. Stories can be so powerful - they can teach us, motivate us, and bring us together. 
[D4:25] Jolene: I also read a recent story about someone who became successful despite facing numerous challenges. It really showed me that anything is possible if you believe and work hard.
[D4:26] Deborah: That's a really powerful message. It reminds me of someone special and their grace and strength when they faced hardships. Check out this creation!
[D4:26] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a bouquet of flowers in a vase on a table
[D4:27] Jolene: Wow, Deb! That's beautiful! Can you tell me the backstory of that bouquet?
[D4:28] Deborah: My friend gave me this bouquet when I was struggling, and it gives me hope and courage. I'm filled with warmth and appreciation when I look at it.
[D4:29] Jolene: That's really sweet. Such a small thing can make a real difference.
[D4:30] Deborah: It's amazing how something as simple as flowers can make a real difference. Nature sure is beautiful.
[D4:31] Jolene: Where are some of your favorite nature spots?
[D4:32] Deborah: Oh, there's so many great places! My favorite is a park with a forest trail - it's so calming getting lost in nature. Then there's this beach nearby that I love - the sound of the waves and the sand under my feet make me feel all peaceful and happy. Do you have any favorite spots, Jolene?
[D4:33] Jolene: Here's a picture I took on vacation last summer in Bogota. It was so beautiful and calming watching the sunset over the water. It definitely made me appreciate nature's calming power.
[D4:33] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person walking on the beach with a surfboard
[D4:34] Deborah: That sounds great, Jolene. Nature's calming for sure. Guess it helps us forget the daily craziness and find inner peace. No wonder you're a fan! I like to come to this spot by the water near my mom's old house. It's where I reflect on her life and find some peace. Being surrounded by nature helps a lot.
[D4:34] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a small island with a lone boat in the water
[D4:35] Jolene: That's so touching! Do you have any little traditions that you do when you come to reflect on your mom?
[D4:36] Deborah: Do you remember this amulet from her? Whenever I come here, I bring it with me. It's how I feel her love and stay close to her. Holding it brings me comfort.
[D4:36] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman wearing a white shirt and a gold chain necklace
[D4:37] Jolene: It's amazing how something so small can have such a big impact, huh?
[D4:38] Deborah: Yeah, even small things like this can make a big difference. It's a reminder of all the love and strength we have inside, connecting us to people we've lost and comforting us.
[D4:39] Jolene: It can keep them close in our hearts every day.
[D4:40] Deborah: Anna also has a pendant that she wears in memory of her mother! This also brought us closer.
[D4:41] Jolene: It's nice to have those reminders as a source of strength when we need it.

[D4:43] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! Your encouragement means a lot to me. I'll definitely stay in touch. Bye, take care and keep shining!
[D4:44] Deborah: Stay safe!  Bye!
Session date: 9:03 pm on 9 February, 2023
[D5:1] Jolene: Hey Deborah! Been a few days since we last talked so I wanted to fill you in on something cool. Last Wednesday I did a mini retreat to assess where I'm at in life. It was a dope experience that totally gave me a new outlook.
[D5:2] Deborah: Hey Jolene! Sounds great. Taking time to reflect can be really awesome. Did you gain any new insights from it?
[D5:3] Jolene: Yep! I achieved so much more than I imagined. It was a real confidence boost.
[D5:4] Deborah: You deserve credit for stepping outside your comfort zone and believing in yourself. What cool stuff did you accomplish at the retreat?
[D5:5] Jolene: I really accomplished something with my engineering project - I came up with some neat solutions and I'm really excited about it.
[D5:6] Deborah: Let's go into more detail.
[D5:7] Jolene:  Green tech could really make a difference in disadvantaged areas. I'd like to look into it and see how I can contribute. Hey, speaking of helping out, I had an idea: a volunteer program where engineers teach STEM to underprivileged kids. What do you think of that?
[D5:8] Deborah: That sounds great, Jolene! It's a great way to help and inspire others. They would benefit a lot from your knowledge. Have you thought of a plan yet?
[D5:9] Jolene: Haven't finished planning yet but I'm thinking of teaming up with local schools/centers to do workshops. We could even invite engineers as guest speakers to show kids their career options.
[D5:10] Deborah: Having guest speakers, like them, would definitely give the kids a real-world view. Have you reached out to any schools or centers yet?
[D5:11] Jolene: No, not yet. I want to solidify the plan first. Can't wait to start reaching out, though!
[D5:12] Deborah: That makes sense. I'm excited to hear how you reach out and help those kids. Let me know how it goes!
[D5:13] Jolene: I'll keep you posted! Appreciate the support! Here are my sketches in the planner.
[D5:13] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a notebook with a pen and a notebook with a page of notes
[D5:14] Deborah: Sounds like you're doing great. Let me know if you need more tips or information.
[D5:15] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! If I need anything else, I'll let you know. You're awesome!
[D5:16] Deborah: You're awesome too! Take care!
[D5:17] Jolene: Stay safe!
Session date: 4:12 pm on 22 February, 2023
[D6:1] Jolene: Hey Deborah, totally buzzing! Had a great night out last night - dinner, and drinks with my friends. So glad I got to let my hair down. You?
[D6:1] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a plate of food and a glass of wine
[D6:2] Deborah: Sounds great, Jolene! I just visited this place and it was so calming. Nostalgic too.
[D6:2] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a garden with a bunch of flowers in buckets
[D6:3] Jolene: Wow, those flowers are beautiful! What type are they? It looks so peaceful there.
[D6:4] Deborah: The roses and dahlias bring me peace. I lost a friend last week, so I've been spending time in the garden to find some comfort.
[D6:5] Jolene: Sorry to hear about your friend, Deb. Losing someone can be really tough. How are you holding up?
[D6:6] Deborah: Thanks for the kind words. It's been tough, but I'm comforted by remembering our time together. It reminds me of how special life is.
[D6:7] Jolene: Memories can give us so much comfort and joy.
[D6:8] Deborah: Memories keep our loved ones close. This is the last photo with Karlie which was taken last summer when we hiked. It was our last one. We had such a great time! Every time I see it, I can't help but smile.
[D6:8] Image caption (automatic): a photo of two women are riding on a motorcycle on a dirt road
[D6:9] Jolene: Wow, looks like a great trip! Where else have you traveled?
[D6:10] Deborah: I've been blessed to travel to a few places and Bali last year was one of my favs. It was a gorgeous island that gave me peace, great for yoga.
[D6:10] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a swing on a beach with a blue sky
[D6:11] Jolene: Wow, that's great! Is yoga on the beach a thing? I've been wanting to try it.
[D6:12] Deborah: The sound of the waves and the fresh air is wonderful!
[D6:13] Jolene: I'll definitely give it a go! It sounds peaceful. Thanks!
[D6:14] Deborah: Let me know how it goes. Enjoy it!
[D6:15] Jolene: I'll keep you posted if I decide to go there.
[D6:16] Deborah: Take care!
Session date: 4:50 pm on 25 February, 2023
[D7:1] Jolene: Hi Deborah, it's been a while! Since we last talked, so much has happened. Balancing engineering school with my partner's video games is quite a feat. But I'm also setting aside time for myself, doing yoga and meditation. It helps give me calm amidst the craziness.
[D7:2] Deborah: Hey Jolene! Great to hear from you. Taking a break is key. How have those practices been helping with everything?
[D7:3] Jolene: They seriously saved me. I chill out and gain perspective when I do yoga. Afterward, I'm more alert and motivated. Here is my last photo.
[D7:3] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman sitting on a yoga mat doing a yoga pose
[D7:4] Deborah: Wow, cool that yoga has been helping you out! Do they also do yoga with you? Does your partner do yoga with you?
[D7:5] Jolene: He started joining me sometimes, which is nice for bonding and relaxing. It's brought us closer. This is just our random photo.
[D7:5] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a man and a woman holding hands with rings on them
[D7:6] Deborah: Aw, that's wonderful! How long have you been married?
[D7:7] Jolene: We're not married yet but we've been together for three years. We're taking it slow and loving the ride. This ring on his hand is just a decoration, not a wedding ring.
[D7:8] Deborah: Sounds nice, Jolene. Enjoying the journey is the main thing. So, how did you two meet?
[D7:9] Jolene: We actually met in an engineering class in college and quickly became friends. It eventually blossomed into something more and it's been great!
[D7:9] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a book and a calculator on a table
[D7:10] Deborah: Wow, your relationship started from a strong friendship. Do you still enjoy working on engineering projects together?
[D7:11] Jolene: Yep, teaming up for these projects feels great! We get each other's struggles and both love it.
[D7:11] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a group of men standing in front of a building
[D7:12] Deborah: Have yoga or meditation helped with any stress?
[D7:13] Jolene: Whenever I'm overwhelmed, I just take a break and do some breathing or meditate. It really helps me feel calmer and clearer, so I'm able to handle challenges more easily.
[D7:14] Deborah: It's been great to see your progress since we last chatted - keep it up!
[D7:15] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! Your support really means a lot. I'm gonna keep pushing forward and continue taking time for myself.

Session date: 4:06 pm on 23 January, 2023
[D1:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene, nice to meet you! How's your week going? Anything fun happened?
[D1:2] Jolene: Hi Deb! Good to meet you! Yeah, my week's been busy. I finished an electrical engineering project last week - took a lot of work, but it's done now. Anything fun happening for you?
[D1:3] Deborah: Congrats! Last week I visited a place that holds a lot of memories for me. It was my mother`s old house.
[D1:4] Jolene: Why does it hold such special memories for you?
[D1:5] Deborah: It was full of memories, she passed away a few years ago. This is our last photo together.
[D1:5] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman in a wheelchair hugging a woman in a wheelchair
[D1:6] Jolene: Sorry about your loss, Deb. My mother also passed away last year. This is my room in her house, I also have many memories there. Is there anything special about it you remember?
[D1:6] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a room with a bench and a window
[D1:7] Deborah: My mom's house had a special bench near the window. She loved to sit there every morning and take in the view. I come to sit here sometimes, it helps me stay connected to her.
[D1:8] Jolene: Staying connected is super important. Do you have something to remember her by? This pendant reminds me of my mother, she gave it to me in 2010  in Paris.
[D1:8] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a heart shaped pendant with a bird on it
[D1:9] Deborah: Yes, I also have a pendant that reminds me of my mother. And what is special for you about your jewelry?
[D1:10] Jolene: It has a special symbol on it that represents freedom for me. It's a nice reminder to go for my goals and not get held back.
[D1:11] Deborah: It should really give you strength and energy!
[D1:12] Jolene: Do you have goals?
[D1:13] Deborah: One of my goals is to keep teaching yoga and supporting my community. I'm passionate about helping people find peace and joy through it.
[D1:14] Jolene: What inspired you to go down this route?
[D1:15] Deborah: Yoga helped me find peace during a rough time, and now I'm passionate about sharing that with others.
[D1:16] Jolene: It is truly inspiring!
[D1:17] Deborah: Gotta run, bye!
[D1:18] Jolene: Looking forward to the next chat!
Session date: 9:49 am on 27 January, 2023
[D2:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene, sorry to tell you this but my dad passed away two days ago. It's been really tough on us all - his sudden death left us all kinda shell-shocked. I'm trying to channel my grief by spending more time with family and cherishing the memories. These moments remind me to live life fully.
[D2:1] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman hugging a woman who is sitting on a couch
[D2:2] Jolene: Sorry to hear about your dad, Deborah. Losing a parent is tough - how's it going for you and your family?
[D2:3] Deborah: Even though it's hard, it's comforting to look back on the great memories. We looked at the family album. Photos give me peace during difficult times. This is my parents' wedding in 1993.
[D2:3] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a bride and groom posing for a picture
[D2:4] Jolene: They were a beautiful couple!
[D2:5] Deborah: My husband and I are trying to be as good a family as my parents were!
[D2:6] Jolene: What do you value in your relationship?
[D2:7] Deborah: It is love, and openness that have kept us close all these years. Being there for each other has made us both happy. Look what letter I received yesterday!
[D2:7] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a note written to someone on a piece of paper
[D2:8] Jolene: What touching words! Who is this letter from?
[D2:9] Deborah: The group members sent this to me! They thanked me for the positive influence I had on them. Those moments remind me why I'm so passionate about yoga.
[D2:10] Jolene: Where do you most often do yoga?
[D2:11] Deborah: This is one of the places where I do it.
[D2:11] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a living room with a television and a window
[D2:12] Jolene: Where is it?
[D2:13] Deborah: That's my old home. I go there now and then for my mom, who passed away. Sitting in that spot by the window gives me peace.
[D2:14] Jolene: Must be great to have that place where you feel connected to her.
[D2:15] Deborah: Yeah, it's special. I can feel her presence when I sit there and it comforts me.
[D2:15] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a window seat in a room with a window
[D2:16] Jolene: Wow, it sounds like that spot holds a lot of sentimental value. Does it bring back any special memories?
[D2:17] Deborah: Yeah, Jolene. She'd sit there every night with a book and a smile, reading was one of her hobbies. It was one of her favorite places in the house. 
[D2:17] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a view of the sky from an airplane window
[D2:18] Jolene: What other hobbies did your mother have?
[D2:19] Deborah: Travel was also her great passion!
[D2:20] Jolene: I want to show you one of my snakes! They always calm me down and make me happy. This is Susie.
[D2:20] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a bed with a snake head sticking out of it
[D2:21] Deborah: Having a pet totally brightens up your life. It's great that it brings you comfort. Do you have any fun moments with your pet that you'd like to share?
[D2:22] Jolene:  I was playing video games and my pet just slinked out of her cage and coiled up next to me - it was too funny! My second snake Seraphim did it. Look at her sly eyes!
[D2:22] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a snake sticking its head out of a blanket
[D2:23] Deborah: Awww, that's so nice! 
[D2:24] Jolene: I bought it a year ago in Paris.
[D2:25] Deborah: Cool, Jolene! Pets bring so much happiness!
[D2:26] Jolene: They are very unusual pets! Here's me and my partner gaming last week - it's so fun. We played the game "Detroit" on the console. We are both crazy about this activity!
[D2:26] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person laying in bed with a dog watching tv
[D2:27] Deborah: Did your boyfriend teach you to play?
[D2:28] Jolene: Even as a child I learned to play on my own.
[D2:29] Deborah: Do you only play old games or try new ones?
[D2:30] Jolene: We are planning to play "Walking Dead" next Saturday.
[D2:31] Deborah: Take care and keep spreading those good vibes!
[D2:32] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! You too, take care. See ya!
Session date: 7:03 pm on 1 February, 2023
[D3:1] Jolene: Hi Deb! How're you? I've been busy. My engineering professor gave us a huge robotics project. It's tough but fun, it's making me get creative and problem-solve.
[D3:1] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a table with a robot on it and a laptop
[D3:2] Deborah: Hey Jolene! It's great to hear from you. It sounds challenging but interesting! It must be really putting your creative and problem-solving skills to the test. How did you feel when you first received the project? Are you enjoying working on it?
[D3:3] Jolene: When I got it, I felt a mix of emotions - excited and nervous. But now, I'm really enjoying it! It's like trying to solve a puzzle, figuring out the best design and programming. Seeing the robot come together is awesome too!

[D23:3] Jolene: This country was awesome! It showed me different kinds of yoga and their backgrounds, which made me appreciate it even more. We visited a lot of delicious cafes! Have you ever been somewhere that was important to you?
[D23:4] Deborah: Yep, last month I visited my mom`s house which holds a special place in my heart. My mom had good and bad times there, but it's still a symbol of her strength and the love she shared with me. This is my husband in front of this house.
[D23:4] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a man standing in front of a house
[D23:5] Jolene: What was it like?
[D23:6] Deborah: It brought back fond memories as I relaxed outside.
[D23:7] Jolene: Sounds great! So glad you have a place to relax and find peace.
[D23:8] Deborah: Thanks, Jolene. It's special for me. How about you? Is there a place that helps you relax?
[D23:9] Jolene: I go to this nearby place to meditate by a tranquil spot.
[D23:9] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a pond with lily pads and a tree in the background
[D23:10] Deborah: Looks chill. What's been the effect of that?
[D23:11] Jolene: It helps me make sense of everything and relieves stress. It's like a restart.
[D23:12] Deborah: Cool, glad you found a place to chill. We all need that occasionally. This is one of my favorite spots to ponder and let things go.

[D23:12] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a lake with a few trees in the water
[D23:13] Jolene: Looks great! What made you pick that spot?
[D23:14] Deborah: The soothing vibes and nice views made it ideal for reflecting and letting go.
[D23:15] Jolene: Here is one more photo from Rio de Janeiro. We went on many excursions there.
[D23:15] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a group of people walking up a set of stairs
[D23:16] Deborah: Wow, those stairs look cool! Where were they taken?
[D23:17] Jolene: We had a great time visiting an old temple. The stairs were amazing!
[D23:18] Deborah: Wow, exploring those temples must have been incredible! Three years ago I was also in Rio de Janeiro, I took a beautiful photo on one of the excursions.
[D23:18] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a large stone structure with a mountain in the background
[D23:19] Jolene: The architecture and history of it all were really interesting. I'm sure you also liked the places you visited there!
[D23:20] Deborah: Exploring historical places and learning their stories is so fun. It was a great experience. I want to share this photo with you.
[D23:20] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a hand holding a piece of paper with writing on it
[D23:21] Jolene:  By the way, what did that paper have written on it in the photo?
[D23:22] Deborah: This was written to me by a friend who, unfortunately, will never be able to support me. I miss him here. This quote says"Let go of what no longer serves you."
[D23:23] Jolene: I'm sorry! That's a good reminder to stay focused and let go of what no longer serves us. Remember the quote in my notebook? It also inspires me!
[D23:23] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a notebook with a quote on it
[D23:24] Deborah: What other quotes give you strength?
[D23:25] Jolene: I came across this one while browsing and it really hit home with me. It's a great reminder to ditch the negative stuff and focus on growing and being positive.
[D23:25] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a notebook with a pen and a plant on a table
[D23:26] Deborah: Surrounding ourselves with good stuff and striving to improve is key.
[D23:27] Jolene: Yep, Deborah! It's about creating a good atmosphere to help us grow and improve. By the way, I have a new plant.
[D23:27] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a plant in a pot on a patio
[D23:28] Deborah: What made you pick it?
[D23:29] Jolene: I got this as a reminder to nurture myself and embrace fresh starts.
[D23:30] Deborah: Nice job, Jolene! Take care of yourself and embrace new beginnings.
[D23:31] Jolene: Thanks Deb! Will do. Good talking to you. Take care!
[D23:32] Deborah: Have a great day!
Session date: 2:14 pm on 3 September, 2023
[D24:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene, just catching up. I went to a cool event last week with the aim to support each other - pretty inspiring. Have you been connecting with anyone lately?
[D24:2] Jolene: Hey Deb, great to hear from you! I've been focusing on studying and my relationship with my partner. We're taking little trips to the beach, it's a great way to relax. How about you, anything new going on?
[D24:3] Deborah: I was busy too - went to a community meetup last Friday. We shared stories and it was nice to feel how connected we are. It made me think about how important relationships are. How about you, how are things going in that area?
[D24:4] Jolene: I'm really thankful for my significant other right now. It's great to have someone encouraging my goals! How are things with your friends and family? Any updates on that front?
[D24:5] Deborah: Relationships with family and friends are so vital. My yoga pals have been my second family - we've held each other up through a lot. The other day I found this old photo. That was when I first started doing yoga. My mum was my biggest fan and source of motivation. She'd often come to my classes with me.
[D24:5] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman sitting on a yoga mat with two children
[D24:6] Jolene: Our loved ones sure are supportive! When I was 10, my parents got me that and it was the start of my passion for video games.
[D24:6] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a nintendo game console and a game controller
[D24:7] Deborah: Cool that they shared that with you. Did you learn on your own or did they teach you?
[D24:8] Jolene: I taught myself, but my dad was always supportive and my mom would play games with me. 
[D24:8] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a nintendo wii game system with a game on the screen
[D24:9] Deborah: That's awesome! Sounds like you had a lot of support from your parents. What was your favorite game to play with mom?
[D24:10] Jolene: One of my favorites was "Monster Hunter: World". The immersive story and open-world gaming are amazing!
[D24:11] Deborah:  It can be so freeing when you get immersed in a game like that. 
[D24:12] Jolene: Yeah! It's my way to de-stress and take a break from life.
[D24:13] Deborah: What's up this month? Anything fun happening for you?
[D24:14] Jolene: Got a lot of finals coming up this month, so I've been studying real hard. It's been quite stressful, but it'll be worth it in the end. Thinking about taking a trip somewhere to relax and recharge afterward.
[D24:15] Deborah: Good luck with it! Let me know if there's anything I can do to assist you.
Session date: 8:31 pm on 6 September, 2023
[D25:1] Jolene: Woohoo! I signed up for a meditation course at a retreat near a lake. Can't wait to share this experience with my partner and learn some new techniques. Sooo excited!
[D25:1] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a building with a curved roof on a hill
[D25:2] Deborah: That`s awesome! It looks so calm in the pic - I hope you enjoy your experience and learn some new techniques!
[D25:3] Jolene:  It's amazing how something so easy can make such a big difference to our health!
[D25:4] Deborah: Yep, it's become part of my routine now. Can't imagine my life without it.

[D21:10] Jolene: Thanks, Deb! Your support means a lot to me. 
[D21:11] Deborah: No problem. You got this! 
[D21:12] Jolene:  I'm not giving up, just gonna keep pushing forward.
[D21:13] Deborah: Reach for your goals and don't forget to enjoy the journey. 
[D21:14] Jolene: Thanks, Deb. Your support means a lot. I'll keep pushing forward and remember to enjoy every step of the way.
[D21:15] Deborah: Come on! The journey's as important as the destination. Take time for yourself and find joy in it. We believe in you!
[D21:15] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a field of sunflowers with a sunset in the background
[D21:16] Jolene: Yeah, you're right! I'll take your advice and find joy on the way. Cheers for the support!
[D21:16] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a city skyline at sunset with a body of water
[D21:17] Deborah: Always by your side!
Session date: 5:33 pm on 26 August, 2023
[D22:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene, since we talked I've been thinking about my mom's influence. Remembering those we love is important.
[D22:2] Jolene: I understand, Deb. Remembering and cherishing the memories of our loved ones is so important. It's comforting to know that their influence still guides us. Last Friday, my partner and I talked about how our loved ones have influenced us and what their values meant to us. It was an emotional chat, but it made us feel closer and showed us what really matters. 
[D22:3] Deborah: Those types of conversations really help build relationships. Can you tell me more about the values they have given you?
[D22:4] Jolene: Definitely! Our loved ones have taught us to persevere and stay resilient, like my mom always said to never give up, and my partner's dad showed them to stay determined. Their values have influenced us to pursue our goals, such as me with engineering and my partner with their creative endeavors. Even though they're not here, we both feel their values encouraging us along our paths.
[D22:5] Deborah: That's wonderful to hear, Jolene! It's amazing how their values continue to guide you, even in their absence. It sounds like you and your partner are honoring their memory by pursuing your respective passions. Have you ever considered incorporating those values into your work as well?
[D22:6] Jolene: Yeah, Deborah! We've been figuring out how to add these values into our projects. As an engineering student, I want to use my talents to do good and help solve important problems. I'm keen on coming up with new ideas and making things more efficient to make the world a better place. Going further, my mom stressed the value of helping others and that's something I want to keep in mind for my engineering projects.
[D22:7] Deborah: When our work ties into our values, it becomes more meaningful. What goals or ideas do you have for incorporating those values into your future projects?
[D22:8] Jolene: In the future, I'm aiming to work on projects that make a real difference to communities. I'm interested in sustainable initiatives and developing innovative solutions for environmental issues. I also want to get involved with organizations that focus on social causes, using my skills to help out. It's about connecting my passion for engineering with my commitment to making a positive impact.
[D22:9] Deborah: You've got a lot of amazing plans for the future. Which projects are you most interested in getting involved in?
[D22:10] Jolene: I'm keen on two projects in particular. One is focused on developing renewable energy, like solar, to help communities and reduce dependence on non-renewables. 
[D22:11] Deborah: Wow Jolene, that's really inspiring!
[D22:12] Jolene: The other is finding ways to supply clean water to those with limited access. Both align with my beliefs about sustainability and assisting those in need. I still have so much to figure out before beginning, but I'm up for the challenge.
[D22:13] Deborah: Sounds great, Jolene! Research is key to success. Little steps and being up for challenges make you stronger. I'm here for you. Connecting to yourself helps tackle any issue. Here's a photo that reminds me of the beauty of nature during a yoga session.
[D22:13] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman doing a yoga pose on the beach
[D22:14] Jolene: It helps with challenges, giving balance and strength. Any tips for staying relaxed while studying?
[D22:15] Deborah: Taking breaks, doing some stretching/yoga, or just going for a walk is really helpful. And don't forget to get enough sleep and take time for self-care. Finding a balance between work and taking care of yourself is important. What self-care activities have you been doing lately?
[D22:16] Jolene: I've been into yoga and meditation lately. It helps me recharge. Doing different poses relieves tension and calms my mind. I've already shared my newfound love for yoga with my partner, and we're planning to go on a meditation retreat together to enhance our practice together.
[D22:16] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman in a pink shirt doing a yoga pose
[D22:17] Deborah: Glad to hear that yoga is helping you rest and recharge. It's great for reflection and self-care. Do your snakes also enjoy it?
[D22:18] Jolene: My snakes just like watching me chill. But she's a great company and always brings a sense of calm.
[D22:19] Deborah: Having a pet around is such a calming feeling. They sure can bring a great sense of comfort. I still have cats, Luna is sitting on the left.
[D22:19] Image caption (automatic): a photo of two cats sitting on a window sill looking out
[D22:20] Jolene: Aww, that's adorable! What's the second one's name?
[D22:21] Deborah: Max! They bring lots of joy and peace to our home.
[D22:21] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a brown leather chair and a black and white floor
[D22:22] Jolene: How did you get them?
[D22:23] Deborah: Max is my mother's cat, I took him when my mother passed away.
[D22:23] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a car with a fan and a mesh bag
[D22:24] Jolene: You're great for taming him. How did you get Luna?
[D22:25] Deborah: I took Luna from the shelter.
[D22:26] Jolene: It’s wonderful that you have become their loving owner!
[D22:27] Deborah: Yes, I really love cats, and they also need a home, love, and care! Moreover, Max is already old, he is 8 years old.
[D22:28] Jolene: How old is Luna?
[D22:29] Deborah: She is younger, she is 5 years old.
[D22:30] Jolene: I am proud of your action to tame these pets!

messages.content: You translate natural-language questions into conjunctive graph queries. You always answer with a single JSON object and nothing else.

Generate up to 2 distinct candidate query plans for the question.

Each plan is a positive conjunctive query. Variables start with "?" and the
literal answer variable "?x" must occur in at least one atom. Each atom has a
short relation, subject and object. The `relation` field contains ONLY the
predicate phrase: write `{"relation": "create", "subject": "Asha",
"object": "?x"}`, never `{"relation": "create(Asha, ?x)", ...}`.
Use at most 4 atoms per plan.

Order plans from most faithful to least preferred:
1. A minimal direct plan only when every requirement can be expressed by one fact. Keep
   qualifiers such as "recently", "after the accident" or "during the workshop"
   inside that relation phrase. Never remove a person, time, place, reason or
   other condition merely because a broader atom is easier to match.
2. A chain plan only when an unnamed intermediate entity must genuinely be found.
3. An intersection plan only when the same answer must independently satisfy
   two relations.

Plans must be meaningfully different. Never pad a plan with artificial atoms such
as recent(?x, true), after(?x, event), type_of(?x, requested_type), or an atom
unconnected to the answer path. Never use true, false or yes as an argument.
Preserve relation direction. For "What has Alice bought?", use buy(Alice, ?x).
Use aggregation "set" for all matching members, "count" for a count, and "none"
for one value. max/min/compare are allowed descriptions but are not executable.

Return JSON exactly in this shape:
{"plans": [
  {"answer_var": "x",
    "atoms": [{"relation": "...", "subject": "...", "object": "?x"}],
    "expected_type": "person|place|date|organization|work|number|other",
    "aggregation": "none|set|max|min|compare|count",
    "fallback": "keyword query"}
]}

Synthetic examples follow. Learn their STRUCTURE; do not copy their entity names
or predicates into the answer. Return fewer than 2 plans when additional
plans would merely be padding. When the question has a genuine intermediate entity,
multiple independent conditions, or an ambiguous predicate, provide at least two
faithful alternatives when possible.

Example 1 — a direct fact needs one plan, not an invented chain.
Question: "Which instrument does Nira play?"
{"plans":[{"answer_var":"x","atoms":[{"relation":"play","subject":"Nira","object":"?x"}],"expected_type":"other","aggregation":"none","fallback":"Nira instrument play"}]}

Example 2 — a real chain uses an unknown intermediate entity.
Question: "In which city is the laboratory led by Omar located?"
{"plans":[{"answer_var":"x","atoms":[{"relation":"lead","subject":"Omar","object":"?y"},{"relation":"located in","subject":"?y","object":"?x"}],"expected_type":"place","aggregation":"none","fallback":"Omar laboratory city"}]}

Example 3 — an intersection repeats the answer variable because both conditions
must describe the same answer.
Question: "Which researcher works at Northstar Institute and studies coral bleaching?"
{"plans":[{"answer_var":"x","atoms":[{"relation":"work at","subject":"?x","object":"Northstar Institute"},{"relation":"study","subject":"?x","object":"coral bleaching"}],"expected_type":"person","aggregation":"set","fallback":"Northstar researcher coral bleaching"}]}

Example 4 — event context stays in the main predicate. It does not become
`after(?x, conference)` or a boolean atom, and it must not be dropped.
Question: "What exhibition did Jun visit after the conference?"
{"plans":[{"answer_var":"x","atoms":[{"relation":"visit after conference","subject":"Jun","object":"?x"}],"expected_type":"other","aggregation":"none","fallback":"Jun exhibition after conference"}]}

Example 5 — plural enumeration uses set; one witness may prove one member.
Question: "Which dishes did Mateo cook for the festival?"
{"plans":[{"answer_var":"x","atoms":[{"relation":"cook for festival","subject":"Mateo","object":"?x"}],"expected_type":"other","aggregation":"set","fallback":"Mateo festival dishes"}]}

Example 6 — counting retrieves the members to count; the number is not an
invented graph constant.
Question: "How many apprentices joined the observatory?"
{"plans":[{"answer_var":"x","atoms":[{"relation":"join","subject":"?x","object":"the observatory"}],"expected_type":"number","aggregation":"count","fallback":"observatory apprentices joined"}]}

Remember: every response is one JSON object with only the `plans` field and the
plan fields shown above. Do not include explanations, markdown or the examples.


The graph was built from the corpus and already contains these relations. Prefer one of them, with its exact spelling, whenever it expresses what the question asks. Invent a new relation only when none of them fits:
  reminded of; remember; reminds to be; has new details for; remind; keep in mind; has memory; cultivate self-awareness; keep updated; wear pendant in memory of; have memory; plans to; bring back; have milestone; stay mindful; is going to; symbolize; get clarity; grow and learn; recharge; look forward; stay focused; realize; plan to take; have plans; focus on; start learning; know; plan to play; have schedule for; reminisce with; focus; special meaning; is busy; take care; deal; excited for; finish; think of; learn
Entity names that exist in the graph, useful as constants:

Session date: 11:46 am on 30 August, 2023
[D23:3] Jolene: This country was awesome! It showed me different kinds of yoga and their backgrounds, which made me appreciate it even more. We visited a lot of delicious cafes! Have you ever been somewhere that was important to you?
[D23:4] Deborah: Yep, last month I visited my mom`s house which holds a special place in my heart. My mom had good and bad times there, but it's still a symbol of her strength and the love she shared with me. This is my husband in front of this house.
[D23:4] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a man standing in front of a house
[D23:5] Jolene: What was it like?
[D23:6] Deborah: It brought back fond memories as I relaxed outside.
[D23:7] Jolene: Sounds great! So glad you have a place to relax and find peace.
[D23:8] Deborah: Thanks, Jolene. It's special for me. How about you? Is there a place that helps you relax?
[D23:9] Jolene: I go to this nearby place to meditate by a tranquil spot.
[D23:9] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a pond with lily pads and a tree in the background
[D23:10] Deborah: Looks chill. What's been the effect of that?
[D23:11] Jolene: It helps me make sense of everything and relieves stress. It's like a restart.
[D23:12] Deborah: Cool, glad you found a place to chill. We all need that occasionally. This is one of my favorite spots to ponder and let things go.

[D23:12] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a lake with a few trees in the water
[D23:13] Jolene: Looks great! What made you pick that spot?
[D23:14] Deborah: The soothing vibes and nice views made it ideal for reflecting and letting go.
[D23:15] Jolene: Here is one more photo from Rio de Janeiro. We went on many excursions there.
[D23:15] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a group of people walking up a set of stairs
[D23:16] Deborah: Wow, those stairs look cool! Where were they taken?
[D23:17] Jolene: We had a great time visiting an old temple. The stairs were amazing!
[D23:18] Deborah: Wow, exploring those temples must have been incredible! Three years ago I was also in Rio de Janeiro, I took a beautiful photo on one of the excursions.
[D23:18] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a large stone structure with a mountain in the background
[D23:19] Jolene: The architecture and history of it all were really interesting. I'm sure you also liked the places you visited there!
[D23:20] Deborah: Exploring historical places and learning their stories is so fun. It was a great experience. I want to share this photo with you.
[D23:20] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a hand holding a piece of paper with writing on it
[D23:21] Jolene:  By the way, what did that paper have written on it in the photo?
[D23:22] Deborah: This was written to me by a friend who, unfortunately, will never be able to support me. I miss him here. This quote says"Let go of what no longer serves you."
[D23:23] Jolene: I'm sorry! That's a good reminder to stay focused and let go of what no longer serves us. Remember the quote in my notebook? It also inspires me!
[D23:23] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a notebook with a quote on it
[D23:24] Deborah: What other quotes give you strength?
[D23:25] Jolene: I came across this one while browsing and it really hit home with me. It's a great reminder to ditch the negative stuff and focus on growing and being positive.
[D23:25] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a notebook with a pen and a plant on a table
[D23:26] Deborah: Surrounding ourselves with good stuff and striving to improve is key.
[D23:27] Jolene: Yep, Deborah! It's about creating a good atmosphere to help us grow and improve. By the way, I have a new plant.
[D23:27] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a plant in a pot on a patio
[D23:28] Deborah: What made you pick it?
[D23:29] Jolene: I got this as a reminder to nurture myself and embrace fresh starts.
[D23:30] Deborah: Nice job, Jolene! Take care of yourself and embrace new beginnings.
[D23:31] Jolene: Thanks Deb! Will do. Good talking to you. Take care!
[D23:32] Deborah: Have a great day!
Session date: 2:14 pm on 3 September, 2023
[D24:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene, just catching up. I went to a cool event last week with the aim to support each other - pretty inspiring. Have you been connecting with anyone lately?
[D24:2] Jolene: Hey Deb, great to hear from you! I've been focusing on studying and my relationship with my partner. We're taking little trips to the beach, it's a great way to relax. How about you, anything new going on?
[D24:3] Deborah: I was busy too - went to a community meetup last Friday. We shared stories and it was nice to feel how connected we are. It made me think about how important relationships are. How about you, how are things going in that area?
[D24:4] Jolene: I'm really thankful for my significant other right now. It's great to have someone encouraging my goals! How are things with your friends and family? Any updates on that front?
[D24:5] Deborah: Relationships with family and friends are so vital. My yoga pals have been my second family - we've held each other up through a lot. The other day I found this old photo. That was when I first started doing yoga. My mum was my biggest fan and source of motivation. She'd often come to my classes with me.
[D24:5] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman sitting on a yoga mat with two children
[D24:6] Jolene: Our loved ones sure are supportive! When I was 10, my parents got me that and it was the start of my passion for video games.
[D24:6] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a nintendo game console and a game controller
[D24:7] Deborah: Cool that they shared that with you. Did you learn on your own or did they teach you?
[D24:8] Jolene: I taught myself, but my dad was always supportive and my mom would play games with me. 
[D24:8] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a nintendo wii game system with a game on the screen
[D24:9] Deborah: That's awesome! Sounds like you had a lot of support from your parents. What was your favorite game to play with mom?
[D24:10] Jolene: One of my favorites was "Monster Hunter: World". The immersive story and open-world gaming are amazing!
[D24:11] Deborah:  It can be so freeing when you get immersed in a game like that. 
[D24:12] Jolene: Yeah! It's my way to de-stress and take a break from life.
[D24:13] Deborah: What's up this month? Anything fun happening for you?
[D24:14] Jolene: Got a lot of finals coming up this month, so I've been studying real hard. It's been quite stressful, but it'll be worth it in the end. Thinking about taking a trip somewhere to relax and recharge afterward.
[D24:15] Deborah: Good luck with it! Let me know if there's anything I can do to assist you.
Session date: 8:31 pm on 6 September, 2023
[D25:1] Jolene: Woohoo! I signed up for a meditation course at a retreat near a lake. Can't wait to share this experience with my partner and learn some new techniques. Sooo excited!
[D25:1] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a building with a curved roof on a hill
[D25:2] Deborah: That`s awesome! It looks so calm in the pic - I hope you enjoy your experience and learn some new techniques!
[D25:3] Jolene:  It's amazing how something so easy can make such a big difference to our health!
[D25:4] Deborah: Yep, it's become part of my routine now. Can't imagine my life without it.

[D19:18] Jolene: Sounds lovely! Nature can be calming. What makes this bench special to you?
[D19:18] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a bench in a park with a tree in the background

[D19:19] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person sitting on a bench in a forest

[D19:24] Jolene: It's so important to cherish it.

[D20:1] Jolene:  Long time no talk! We were given a new game for the console last week, it is Battlefield 1. What's been up with you?
[D20:2] Deborah: Hey Jolene! Good to hear from you. That`s cool! Been thinking about a few big moments lately - went to a place that held a lot of memories for me. Sat on a bench where we used to chat and it brought back a lot of emotions.

[D20:4] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a vase of flowers on the ground in a street

[D20:6] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman holding a bouquet of red roses

[D20:9] Jolene: Wow Deb, that's awesome! We should definitely take time to enjoy that and not let the business of life cause us to miss out on the good stuff.

[D20:12] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a sunset over a body of water

[D20:14] Deborah: Moments like that I'll always cherish.
[D20:15] Jolene: That calm and peaceful feeling is so nice - it's great for recharging and thinking.

[D20:23] Jolene: I'm really finding my zen again!
[D20:24] Deborah: Keep it up!
[D20:25] Jolene: Thanks for your support, Deb!

Session date: 7:03 pm on 1 February, 2023
[D3:4] Deborah: That's awesome, Jolene! You're enjoying the process. It must be really satisfying to see it come together. Keep up the good work! Oh, by the way, I met my new neighbor Anna yesterday!
[D3:4] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a yellow sign with a picture of a family
[D3:5] Jolene: How did you two meet?
[D3:6] Deborah: It happened at yoga in the park.
[D3:7] Jolene: Wow, that's awesome! It's great connecting with people who have similar interests. Did you two talk about it?
[D3:8] Deborah: Yeah, we talked about how it has improved our lives and the sense of community it gives.
[D3:9] Jolene: Sounds great!
[D3:9] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a purse with a plant on a table
[D3:10] Deborah: Have you ever thought about resuming yoga?
[D3:11] Jolene: Well... we planned to play the console with my partner.
[D3:12] Deborah: It's also good that you have something to do together.
[D3:13] Jolene: Thanks for the kind words!
[D3:14] Deborah: Gotta run bye!
[D3:15] Jolene: See you soon!
Session date: 9:48 am on 4 February, 2023
[D4:1] Jolene: Hey Deborah! Good to hear from you. How've you been? I've been on an emotional rollercoaster lately, but I'm coping.
[D4:2] Deborah: Hey Jolene! Good to hear from you. All good here - how about you? Anything new happening lately?
[D4:3] Jolene: I had a major milestone last week and it went really well - I'm so relieved and proud. It was a huge accomplishment for me as an engineer.
[D4:4] Deborah: That's awesome. You must have worked really hard for that. I'm so proud of you. Care to share more about it?
[D4:5] Jolene: Thanks so much! I had to plan and research a lot to design and build a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need. It was tough, but I loved the experience.
[D4:6] Deborah: Your engineering skills really made a difference for people in a rural area. That's amazing! How did it feel when you saw it working?
[D4:7] Jolene: It was such a surreal moment. Seeing it working and providing clean water to the community was incredibly satisfying. It reminded me of how engineering can make a difference in people's lives. It made me feel like I had a purpose and had done something good.
[D4:8] Deborah: So, what are your career aspirations now?
[D4:9] Jolene:  I want to keep working in engineering and continue to make a positive impact on communities in need by creating sustainable solutions. My goal is to contribute towards making the world a better place with my work.
[D4:10] Deborah:  I'm sure great things will keep coming your way. Keep up the good work and follow your passions!
[D4:11] Jolene: Your support means a lot. I'm determined to keep going and make a difference. Your encouragement really motivates me to pursue my passions.
[D4:12] Deborah: When things get tough, just take a deep breath and remember why you're doing this. This is where I spend a lot of my time, teaching yoga. It's a great way to find balance and reconnect with ourselves. I bonded with Anna during yesterday's l yoga class.
[D4:12] Image caption (automatic): a photo of two women in a dance studio doing a dance pose
[D4:13] Jolene: Wow, that's awesome! What new poses did you try?
[D4:14] Deborah: We were trying out different dance poses, like Warrior II, which builds strength and boosts focus.
[D4:14] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman doing a yoga pose on a chair
[D4:15] Jolene: Is it difficult to do?
[D4:16] Deborah: Yes, but this brought us closer to Anna! We supported each other, that means a lot.
[D4:17] Jolene: Can you explain how to do it?
[D4:18] Deborah: Sure! To do this modified pose, sit on the edge of a chair with your feet planted. Twist your torso to one side and use your hand on your knee for support. You'll feel a stretch in your back and shoulders as you hold it for a few breaths, then switch sides. It's great for relaxing tense muscles.
[D4:19] Jolene: Sounds really hard! Here's my bookshelf!
[D4:19] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a book shelf with a lot of books on it
[D4:20] Deborah: That's quite a collection! Have you had a favorite book lately? I'd love to hear your thoughts.
[D4:21] Jolene: Thanks Deborah! I'm really into this book called "Sapiens" - it's a fascinating look at human history and how technology has affected us. It's giving me a lot to think about!
[D4:22] Deborah: Great, this is interesting! Have you come across any recent ones that really struck you?
[D4:23] Jolene: Two weeks ago I read "Avalanche" by Neal Stephenson in one sitting! 
[D4:24] Deborah: That sounds cool, Jolene. Stories can be so powerful - they can teach us, motivate us, and bring us together. 
[D4:25] Jolene: I also read a recent story about someone who became successful despite facing numerous challenges. It really showed me that anything is possible if you believe and work hard.
[D4:26] Deborah: That's a really powerful message. It reminds me of someone special and their grace and strength when they faced hardships. Check out this creation!
[D4:26] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a bouquet of flowers in a vase on a table
[D4:27] Jolene: Wow, Deb! That's beautiful! Can you tell me the backstory of that bouquet?
[D4:28] Deborah: My friend gave me this bouquet when I was struggling, and it gives me hope and courage. I'm filled with warmth and appreciation when I look at it.
[D4:29] Jolene: That's really sweet. Such a small thing can make a real difference.
[D4:30] Deborah: It's amazing how something as simple as flowers can make a real difference. Nature sure is beautiful.
[D4:31] Jolene: Where are some of your favorite nature spots?
[D4:32] Deborah: Oh, there's so many great places! My favorite is a park with a forest trail - it's so calming getting lost in nature. Then there's this beach nearby that I love - the sound of the waves and the sand under my feet make me feel all peaceful and happy. Do you have any favorite spots, Jolene?
[D4:33] Jolene: Here's a picture I took on vacation last summer in Bogota. It was so beautiful and calming watching the sunset over the water. It definitely made me appreciate nature's calming power.
[D4:33] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person walking on the beach with a surfboard
[D4:34] Deborah: That sounds great, Jolene. Nature's calming for sure. Guess it helps us forget the daily craziness and find inner peace. No wonder you're a fan! I like to come to this spot by the water near my mom's old house. It's where I reflect on her life and find some peace. Being surrounded by nature helps a lot.
[D4:34] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a small island with a lone boat in the water
[D4:35] Jolene: That's so touching! Do you have any little traditions that you do when you come to reflect on your mom?
[D4:36] Deborah: Do you remember this amulet from her? Whenever I come here, I bring it with me. It's how I feel her love and stay close to her. Holding it brings me comfort.
[D4:36] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a woman wearing a white shirt and a gold chain necklace
[D4:37] Jolene: It's amazing how something so small can have such a big impact, huh?
[D4:38] Deborah: Yeah, even small things like this can make a big difference. It's a reminder of all the love and strength we have inside, connecting us to people we've lost and comforting us.
[D4:39] Jolene: It can keep them close in our hearts every day.
[D4:40] Deborah: Anna also has a pendant that she wears in memory of her mother! This also brought us closer.
[D4:41] Jolene: It's nice to have those reminders as a source of strength when we need it.

Session date: 3:56 pm on 6 June, 2023
[D13:1] Jolene: Hey Deborah! Long time no talk - I had lots of stuff going on. Remember the tough engineering project? I finally wrapped that up last month. Look at the result!
[D13:1] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a solar powered vehicle with a solar panel on the back
[D13:2] Deborah: Jolene! Congrats on wrapping up your with it! You really put in the work and it paid off. 
[D13:3] Jolene:  I'm really proud of myself for sticking it out despite the problems and finishing it. It's definitely a big milestone.
[D13:4] Deborah: Now that you've reached this big milestone, what do you have planned next?
[D13:5] Jolene:  I'm interning at a well-known engineering firm. It's been a great opportunity to test my skills and gain real-world experience. These are my new colleagues!
[D13:5] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a group of construction workers posing for a picture
[D13:6] Deborah: What's been the best part of it so far?
[D13:7] Jolene: The best part so far has been being able to apply what I learned in school to real projects. It's so fulfilling to see my ideas come to life.
[D13:8] Deborah: Mind if I ask how the internship has impacted you?
[D13:9] Jolene: It has had a positive impact on my life. It has stoked my love of engineering and has encouraged me to keep striving for my dreams.
[D13:10] Deborah:  How has it inspired you to keep striving for your dreams?
[D13:11] Jolene: Hanging out with people who love what they do has really inspired me to stay focused and keep working towards my goals. It's shown me that with dedication and effort, anything is possible.
[D13:12] Deborah: Have you been able to find a good work-life balance during your internship?
[D13:13] Jolene: Honestly, finding that balance has been tough. I've been slogging away and it's been hard to make time for my hobbies and chilling out.
[D13:14] Deborah:  Have you considered taking some breaks and finding activities like yoga to help you relax and unwind? That might make a difference.
[D13:15] Jolene: Yeah, I`m trying to do it. Here's an example of how I spent yesterday morning, yoga on top of mount Talkeetna.
[D13:15] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a man standing on a rock with his arms outstretched
[D13:16] Deborah: Nice job, Jolene! How long have you been doing yoga and meditation? It looks like it's really helping you regroup and recharge.
[D13:17] Jolene: I've been doing them sporadically for about 3 years now and they've had a real positive effect on me.
[D13:18] Deborah: Has it benefited you in any way? Have you found it helpful in difficult moments?
[D13:19] Jolene: It has helped me with stress and kept me centered.
[D13:20] Deborah: Glad they've been helpful for you!
[D13:21] Jolene: No idea how I would've survived without them!
[D13:22] Deborah: This is my favorite studio and it's always so calming. 
[D13:22] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a room with a bench and a window
[D13:23] Jolene:  I was wondering if you have any advice on calming the mind and breathing during yoga?
[D13:24] Deborah: I'd recommend practicing mindful breathing for yoga. Set aside a few minutes each day to sit with your eyes closed, take deep breaths, and focus on how the air feels entering and leaving your body. 
[D13:25] Jolene: Thanks, Deborah! I'll definitely give it a try. Appreciate the advice!
[D13:26] Deborah:  If you need more tips or help, just let me know. Take care!
[D13:27] Jolene: See you!
Session date: 9:17 am on 26 June, 2023

messages.content: You translate natural-language questions into conjunctive graph queries. You always answer with a single JSON object and nothing else.

Generate up to 2 distinct candidate query plans for the question.

Each plan is a positive conjunctive query. Variables start with "?" and the
literal answer variable "?x" must occur in at least one atom. Each atom has a
short relation, subject and object. The `relation` field contains ONLY the
predicate phrase: write `{"relation": "create", "subject": "Asha",
"object": "?x"}`, never `{"relation": "create(Asha, ?x)", ...}`.
Use at most 4 atoms per plan.

Order plans from most faithful to least preferred:
1. A minimal direct plan only when every requirement can be expressed by one fact. Keep
   qualifiers such as "recently", "after the accident" or "during the workshop"
   inside that relation phrase. Never remove a person, time, place, reason or
   other condition merely because a broader atom is easier to match.
2. A chain plan only when an unnamed intermediate entity must genuinely be found.
3. An intersection plan only when the same answer must independently satisfy
   two relations.

Plans must be meaningfully different. Never pad a plan with artificial atoms such
as recent(?x, true), after(?x, event), type_of(?x, requested_type), or an atom
unconnected to the answer path. Never use true, false or yes as an argument.
Preserve relation direction. For "What has Alice bought?", use buy(Alice, ?x).
Use aggregation "set" for all matching members, "count" for a count, and "none"
for one value. max/min/compare are allowed descriptions but are not executable.

Return JSON exactly in this shape:
{"plans": [
  {"answer_var": "x",
    "atoms": [{"relation": "...", "subject": "...", "object": "?x"}],
    "expected_type": "person|place|date|organization|work|number|other",
    "aggregation": "none|set|max|min|compare|count",
    "fallback": "keyword query"}
]}

Synthetic examples follow. Learn their STRUCTURE; do not copy their entity names
or predicates into the answer. Return fewer than 2 plans when additional
plans would merely be padding. When the question has a genuine intermediate entity,

Session date: 7:37 pm on 9 July, 2023
[D15:4] Jolene: Deborah, that's awesome! Being part of a supportive group must be super motivating. Finding a team that's passionate about something makes a huge difference. Just thinking about my own journey too.
[D15:5] Deborah: Having people who can cheer you on and give you advice really makes a difference. What has it been like for you finding supportive folks?
[D15:6] Jolene: Gaming's been tough lately, but I'm grateful I have someone who's also into it. My partner helps me stay focused on our goals. We have a lot of cute photos, I want to share with you.
[D15:6] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a man and a woman sitting in a chair in front of a computer
[D15:7] Deborah:  What do you like best about gaming together?
[D15:8] Jolene: We get to tackle challenges and have a shared experience. It's always a blast when we're into the same game and achieve something tough. Plus, it's a great way to bond and get closer.
[D15:9] Deborah: Woah, that's cool! Gaming is so good for strengthening relationships. Do you two have a favorite game to play together?
[D15:10] Jolene: Yeah, we love playing "It takes two" together! It's a fun team-strategy game and it's competitive. Plus, it's a great way for us to bond. Do you have any activities you like doing with people?
[D15:11] Deborah: Yep, I do running and yoga/meditation with others. Connecting with people and creating a community is great. Plus, I love organizing workshops and events to practice mindfulness and self-care. It's an awesome way to have fun, build relationships, and support each other's growth.
[D15:11] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a group of people doing yoga in a park
[D15:12] Jolene: Sounds like a great way to relax. What do your workshops and events involve?
[D15:13] Deborah: It involves various activities such as yoga, meditation, and self-reflection. They aim to cultivate self-awareness, promote mental and emotional well-being, and help individuals find inner peace. It's a space where people can connect, explore, and grow.
[D15:14] Jolene:  Your events are awesome for helping people connect and learn, it is so important. How has everything been going for you?
[D15:15] Deborah: Thanks, Jolene! It's been great seeing everyone come together and support each other. It's amazing to witness the growth and transformation that happens through these workshops. I'm honored to be a part of it.
[D15:15] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a game board with a bunch of cards on it
[D15:16] Jolene: Wow, Deb! I can imagine how rewarding it must be to create a space for growth and change. It's great to hear that everything's going well. You can always count on me for support! I just want to share a photo with you.
[D15:16] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a snake on a branch with a book
[D15:17] Deborah: Thanks, Jolene! Your support means a lot to me. I'm here for you too. By the way, I noticed your pet in the picture. What made you decide to get a snake?
[D15:18] Jolene:  I was fascinated by reptiles, and it felt like the perfect pet for me. Taking care of it has been really calming, and it's a great way to connect with nature.
[D15:19] Deborah:  Glad you found something that gives you peace and calm. Do you have a favorite memory with "it" to share?
[D15:20] Jolene: I have lots of great memories, like our little 'snake adventure'. She got out and I spent hours searching, so relieved when I finally found her snuggling under the bed. It really showed how much I love her.
[D15:20] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a snake in a tank with sand and plants
[D15:21] Deborah: What was it like when you found her? I can imagine the relief!
[D15:22] Jolene: Seeing her snuggled under the bed made me feel so much love and gratitude. It made me realize how important she is to me.
[D15:23] Deborah: They bring so much joy and remind us of what's important.
[D15:24] Jolene: Animals teach us a lot about love and gratitude, and they bring so much joy. 
[D15:25] Deborah: I haven't introduced you to my pets yet! I don't like dogs, that's why I have cats.
[D15:25] Image caption (automatic): a photography of two cats sitting on a couch with a blanket
[D15:26] Jolene: Looks like they're having a blast! How often do you take them out?
[D15:27] Deborah: Exercise and nature are really important to me, so I make sure to take them out for a run in the park every morning and evening.
[D15:27] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person walking on the beach with a surfboard
[D15:28] Jolene: Wow Deb, that's great! I'd love to experience that every day.
[D15:29] Deborah: Nature helps me find peace every day - it's so refreshing!
[D15:30] Jolene: It's a pity that my snakes don't run!  I'd love to do that more often. They would motivate me and together it would be more fun.
[D15:30] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person walking on the beach with a surfboard
[D15:31] Deborah:  It's like hitting a reset button that helps me put things into perspective and gives me time to reflect.
[D15:32] Jolene: Yeah, I totally get it. Whenever I can, I love going for walks to take it all in. And I take photos like this
[D15:32] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a sunset over a body of water
[D15:33] Deborah: It's amazing how nature has the power to bring us peace and clarity.
[D15:34] Jolene: This photo captures the peacefulness of a lake surrounded by trees.
[D15:34] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a dock on a lake with trees in the background
[D15:35] Deborah: Why did you choose that spot? It looks so calm.
[D15:36] Jolene: It's such a hidden gem! It makes me feel so peaceful and tranquil.
[D15:37] Deborah: Lucky you for having somewhere to relax and tune out!
[D15:38] Jolene: We'll definitely go there together sometime!
[D15:39] Deborah: We all need a timeout!
Session date: 9:26 am on 1 August, 2023
[D16:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene! Great news - I just started a project for a cleanup in our community and have been trying to raise funds for it. It's been amazing to see everyone come together to make a difference. How've you been? Anything new going on?
[D16:2] Jolene: Hey Debs! Congrats on your project for the community! As for me, life's been a rollercoaster lately. Last week, I had a huge setback with my project. I put in so much work and it all crashed and I lost everything. SO frustrating and depressing.
[D16:3] Deborah: Jolene, sorry to hear that. It must be really tough. I'm here for you and if I can do anything, just let me know. Is there anything that's helping you cope?
[D16:4] Jolene: Your support means a lot. Susie really helps when times get tough. Pets have been great company. Video games have also been a nice distraction.
[D16:4] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a man holding a snake on his arm
[D16:5] Deborah: They can really provide love and comfort, especially during tough times. How did you come to have Susie?
[D16:6] Jolene: I adopted her two years ago when I was feeling lonely and wanted some company.
[D16:7] Deborah: That's great, Jolene! Animals sure have a way of bringing us happiness. They understand us and provide us with comfort. Plus, having a pet teaches us responsibility. She came at the perfect time - cherish those moments with her and find strength in her presence.
[D16:8] Jolene: Thanks Deborah. Having her around shows me I can stay strong and find joy in the small stuff.
[D16:9] Deborah: Enjoying the little things is key. Those little moments can give us a boost and push us forward. How have you been taking care of yourself lately?

Session date: 5:35 pm on 22 March, 2023
[D10:7] Deborah: Have you tried breaking it down or prioritizing the tasks?
[D10:8] Jolene: It can often feel overwhelming and difficult to figure out where to start.
[D10:9] Deborah: I get it, Jolene. When I'm overloaded, I use a certain method. It helps me figure out what's important and urgent so I'm more organized. Do you know about it?
[D10:10] Jolene: Nah, I'm not familiar with that one. What's it about?
[D10:11] Deborah: Want me to tell you about it? It helps you organize things based on how important and urgent they are.
[D10:12] Jolene: Sure, tell me more about it! It sounds useful.
[D10:13] Deborah: The Eisenhower Matrix sorts tasks into four boxes, categorizing them based on their urgency and importance. It can be really useful for organizing and prioritizing. Here's a breakdown. 
[D10:13] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a pair of scissors sitting on top of a piece of paper
[D10:14] Jolene: The visualization is helpful too. Thanks for sharing!
[D10:15] Deborah: I am glad, it was helpful. Let's give it a try and see if it helps you stay focused and less stressed. 
[D10:16] Jolene: Yeah, I'll give it a go. Fingers crossed it'll help me. Thanks for the help!
[D10:17] Deborah: Don't forget to take it easy and look after yourself. Wishing you all the best! Recently, Anna and I were sitting by the sea, watching the sunset and talking about each other. And we realized that we inspire each other. What thoughts does the sea in this photo make you think of?
[D10:17] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person walking on the beach with a surfboard
[D10:18] Jolene: This gets me thinking of when I'll learn to surf. Gotta find that spare time!
[D10:19] Deborah: Surfing, huh Jolene? Chase your dreams, don't be daunted. Have you thought about the steps you can take?
[D10:20] Jolene: Definitely! I've been gathering information, watching videos, and I even got a beginners' guide to surfing. Just need to find the right time and place to get a lesson.
[D10:21] Deborah: Way to go! Taking those first steps is key. Believe in yourself and keep going!
[D10:21] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a row of surfboards leaning against a palm tree
[D10:22] Jolene: Thanks for the support! Those got me pumped to try surfing. Gonna keep pushing myself to make it happen.
[D10:23] Deborah: Keep it up, Jolene! Remember, the experience matters just as much as the end result. Step by step and have fun along the way. You can do it!
[D10:24] Jolene: Thanks for the boost!
Session date: 4:03 pm on 28 March, 2023
[D11:1] Jolene: Hey Deb, long time no talk. A lot's happened! On Friday I had a breakthrough with my engineering project. Finally found a solution to a prob that's been bugging me. Feels great to see my hard work paying off.
[D11:1] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a person's hand holding a pair of scissors
[D11:2] Deborah: You've really proven your skills. Feels great, right? Keep it up! And I bought new props for the yoga class! Here it is in action.
[D11:2] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a group of people doing yoga in a room
[D11:3] Jolene: Oh, I also have new details for this case! Rate it!
[D11:3] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a cardboard mat with a cup of coffee on it
[D11:4] Deborah: That`s cool! I also bought this candle for the atmosphere and to improve my yoga practice. How about you? When you do it, what feelings do you get?
[D11:4] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a candle with a sprig of rosemary on a table
[D11:5] Jolene: I feel relaxed during this activity. I love creating a serene space with soothing scents like lavender and rosemary. Do you have any favorite scents or rituals for when you do it?
[D11:6] Deborah: I'm also a big fan of scents like this! Candles and essential oils add warmth and calm to my yoga session. It's amazing how certain smells can transport you to a place of peace.  Do you have any other ways to enhance your yoga practice?
[D11:7] Jolene: I find music helps me. Any favorite tracks?
[D11:8] Deborah: I find instrumental tracks with mellow melodies and rhythms help create a peaceful vibe. One of my favorites is a track called "Savana." What songs/artists do you like listening to during your practice?
[D11:9] Jolene: I love listening to Nils Frahm and Olafur Arnalds during my practice. Their music is so calming and puts me in a different headspace. Do you have any recommendations for other similar artists or tracks I should check out?
[D11:10] Deborah: Also, I'm listening to an album called 'Sleep,' which is great for meditation and deep relaxation. Hope you find it as calming as I do!
[D11:11] Jolene: Thanks for the tips, Deborah! I'm gonna check them out. It's always good to have some new tunes for yoga!
[D11:12] Deborah:  Let me know your thoughts on the albums!
[D11:13] Jolene: See you!
[D11:14] Deborah: Take care and keep up the good work!
Session date: 4:30 pm on 9 April, 2023
[D12:1] Deborah: Hey Jolene! Great to see you! Had a blast biking nearby with my neighbor last week - was so freeing and beautiful. Checked out an art show with a friend today - really cool and inspiring stuff. Reminded me of my mom.
[D12:1] Image caption (automatic): a photo of a large brown and white photo of a person
[D12:2] Jolene: Hey Deborah! Sounds like you had a blast biking and at the art show. Your photo looks like you were really into it! Did it make you think profound thoughts?
[D12:3] Deborah: My mom was interested in art. She believed art could give out strong emotions and uniquely connect us. When I go to an art show, it's like we're still experiencing it together even though she's gone. It's hard but comforting.
[D12:4] Jolene: Losing someone is hard, but finding something that helps you cope is great.
[D12:5] Deborah: Finding ways to keep her memory alive gives me peace. It's amazing how something simple like artwork can bring back powerful emotions and remind us of those we've lost. It's about finding solace in the things we love, and art has done that for me.
[D12:6] Jolene: Even though my snakes can't chat or understand what I'm going through, our time together is valuable and teaches me to take time and be in tune with myself. Similarly, playing video games with my partner after a long day is a great way for me to relax.
[D12:7] Deborah: Simple things can indeed bring us the most happiness. How have these activities helped you during tough times?
[D12:8] Jolene: It brings us closer together!
[D12:9] Deborah: This kind of comfort can be really helpful when times get tough.
[D12:10] Jolene: Just so you know, I've been working on a big project lately - it's been tough but also really cool to watch it take shape. Can't wait to see the final result!
[D12:11] Deborah: I am waiting to hear how everything turns out. Keep up the good work!
[D12:12] Jolene: Thanks Deb! Your support means a lot. I'll keep you updated on the progress of the project.
[D12:13] Deborah: Glad my support means a lot to you! I'll always be here for you. 
[D12:14] Jolene: Take care!
[D12:15] Deborah: Enjoy your day and make time for the things that bring you joy. See ya!
[D12:16] Jolene:  I'll make sure to find time for that. Have a good one!
